concepts.name: Assets, liabilities, and equity
concepts.summary: Define and recognise assets, liabilities and owner's equity and give examples of each.

concepts.name: The accounting equation
concepts.summary: Explain why assets always equal liabilities plus equity and how a transaction keeps it in balance.

concepts.name: Revenues and expenses
concepts.summary: Distinguish revenues and expenses from assets and liabilities and explain how they change equity.

concepts.name: Business transactions
concepts.summary: Identify which events are recorded as transactions and which are not.

concepts.name: Debits and credits
concepts.summary: State that debit means left and credit means right and know which account types increase with each.

concepts.name: Double-entry principle
concepts.summary: Explain that every transaction affects at least two accounts with total debits equal to total credits.

misconceptions.text: Debit always means an increase and credit always means a decrease.
Equity is the same thing as cash the business holds.
Any event involving the business, such as signing a job offer, must be recorded as a transaction.

concepts.name: Chart of accounts
concepts.summary: Use a chart of accounts to choose the correct account for each part of a transaction.

concepts.name: Journal entries
concepts.summary: Analyse a transaction and record it as a dated, balanced journal entry with a description.

concepts.name: Posting to the ledger
concepts.summary: Transfer journal entries into ledger accounts and calculate running account balances.

concepts.name: Trial balance preparation
concepts.summary: List all ledger balances and check that total debits equal total credits.

concepts.name: Simple income statement
concepts.summary: Prepare an income statement by subtracting expenses from revenues to find net income.

concepts.name: Owner investments and drawings
concepts.summary: Record owner contributions and withdrawals and show their effect on equity separate from revenue and expense.

concepts.name: Simple balance sheet
concepts.summary: Prepare a balance sheet listing assets, liabilities and equity at a date, including retained net income.

misconceptions.text: A balanced trial balance proves that all transactions were recorded correctly.
Owner drawings are an expense that appears on the income statement.
Posting to the ledger is where a transaction is first recorded.

concepts.name: Accrual basis accounting
concepts.summary: Apply the accrual basis so revenue and expenses are recognised when earned or incurred rather than when cash moves.

concepts.name: Revenue recognition and matching
concepts.summary: Analyse when revenue is earned and match expenses to the periods they help generate.

concepts.name: Adjusting entries
concepts.summary: Prepare entries for prepaid expenses, unearned revenue, accrued items and depreciation at period end.

concepts.name: Depreciation of fixed assets
concepts.summary: Calculate and record depreciation and show assets at carrying amount.

concepts.name: Inventory and cost of goods sold
concepts.summary: Record purchases and sales of inventory and calculate cost of goods sold and gross profit.

concepts.name: Closing entries and the cycle
concepts.summary: Analyse how closing entries reset temporary accounts and carry results into retained earnings within the full accounting cycle.

concepts.name: Bank reconciliation and receivables
concepts.summary: Reconcile cash records to bank statements and account for credit sales and uncollectible receivables.

misconceptions.text: Revenue is earned when cash is received.
Depreciation sets aside cash to replace the asset or measures its market value.
Closing entries apply to all accounts including assets and liabilities.

concepts.name: Cash flow statement
concepts.summary: Derive operating, investing and financing cash flows and explain why they differ from net income.

concepts.name: Financial ratio analysis
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret liquidity, profitability and leverage ratios from the statements.

concepts.name: Inventory costing methods
concepts.summary: Compare cost-flow assumptions and judge their effects on profit, assets and taxes.

concepts.name: Accounting estimates and judgment
concepts.summary: Evaluate how estimates for depreciation, bad debts and provisions affect reported results.

concepts.name: Error detection and correction
concepts.summary: Find errors that a trial balance does not reveal and correct them with appropriate entries.

concepts.name: Accounting for equity structures
concepts.summary: Analyse how partnership and corporate equity, dividends and retained earnings are recorded and presented.

concepts.name: Internal controls
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether controls adequately protect assets and the reliability of records.

misconceptions.text: Profitable companies cannot run out of cash.
A ratio is meaningful on its own without comparison to peers or trends.
Accounting figures are objective facts with no judgment involved.

concepts.name: Conceptual framework evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate accounting treatments against relevance, faithful representation and recognition criteria.

concepts.name: Earnings quality assessment
concepts.summary: Judge whether reported earnings reflect sustainable performance or aggressive choices.

concepts.name: Complex transaction treatment
concepts.summary: Determine the appropriate recognition and measurement for transactions such as leases and deferred tax.

concepts.name: Accounting system design
concepts.summary: Design charts of accounts, journals and workflows that fit a business and support reporting and control.

concepts.name: Consolidated reporting concepts
concepts.summary: Assess how group structures determine which entities are combined and how intra-group items are eliminated.

concepts.name: Management reporting frameworks
concepts.summary: Create reporting packs that translate ledger data into decision-useful management information.

misconceptions.text: Following the standards mechanically guarantees a fair presentation.
Legal compliance is the same as high-quality earnings.
Consolidation simply adds together every subsidiary's figures.
